title: Boss: the order pipeline
summary: Combine translator, splitter, router, aggregator, idempotency and a dead letter channel.

steps.title: The brief
body: Acme's warehouse still exports orders as text. You are building the pipeline that turns them into
per-warehouse picking lists, survives duplicate deliveries, and parks what it cannot process.

steps.title: Translate the legacy format
prompt: The warehouse sends one line per book: `ORDER_ID;ISBN;QTY;PRICE_PENCE`, for example `A1;9780131103627;2;1299`.
Write `string Translate(string line)` returning canonical JSON (exact property order, compact):
```json
- trim each field; `price` is pence ÷ 100 as a `decimal`;
- throw `FormatException` if there are not exactly 4 fields, or quantity/pence are not integers, or quantity is not at least 1.
solution: if (!int.TryParse(f[2], out var qty) || qty < 1) throw new FormatException("bad quantity");
if (!int.TryParse(f[3], out var pence)) throw new FormatException("bad price");
return JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { orderId = f[0], isbn = f[1], quantity = qty, price = pence / 100m });
hints: `Split(';')`, trim, check the count, `int.TryParse` both numbers.

steps.title: Picking lists
prompt: Lines from many orders arrive as canonical JSON (as produced above). Each ISBN prefix decides the warehouse:
ISBNs starting `97801` go to `"north"`, everything else to `"south"`. Lines with `quantity` greater than `50` are
bulk orders for the `"bulk"` team instead, whatever their prefix.
Write `Dictionary<string, List<string>> PickingLists(IEnumerable<string> lines)` that **routes** every line and
**aggregates** per destination: each entry is `"{orderId}:{isbn}x{quantity}"`, in arrival order. Only destinations
that received something appear.
solution: if (!result.TryGetValue(dest, out var list)) result[dest] = list = new();
hints: Decide the destination with the bulk check first, then the prefix.
template: Dojo.Eq("north list", new List<string> { "A1:9780131103627x2", "B7:9780134494166x3" }, dojoP.GetValueOrDefault("north") ?? new());
Dojo.Eq("south list", new List<string> { "A1:9781492056355x1" }, dojoP.GetValueOrDefault("south") ?? new());
Dojo.Eq("bulk wins over prefix", new List<string> { "B7:9780134685991x60" }, dojoP.GetValueOrDefault("bulk") ?? new());
Dojo.Eq("no lines -> no lists", 0, PickingLists(new string[0]).Count);

steps.title: Retries, dead letters and duplicates
prompt: Write a class `Pipeline` that delivers messages to a handler with at-least-once semantics handled properly:
- constructor `Pipeline(Func<string, bool> handler, int maxAttempts)`: the handler returns `true` on success, `false` on a (transient) failure.
- `string Deliver(string messageId, string body)`:
- if `messageId` was already delivered successfully → `"duplicate"` (handler not called);
- otherwise call the handler up to `maxAttempts` times until it returns `true` → remember the id and return `"ok after {n}"` (`n` = attempts used);
- if every attempt fails → add `"{messageId}: {body}"` to `DeadLetters` and return `"dead-lettered"`. A dead-lettered id is **not** remembered as delivered, so replaying it later is possible.
- `List<string> DeadLetters` (get-only).
- `string Replay()`: removes every dead letter and delivers each again (in order, using the stored id and body). Returns their results joined with `", "` (empty string if there were none).
starter: public Pipeline(Func<string, bool> handler, int maxAttempts) { }
public string Deliver(string messageId, string body) => "";
solution: public Pipeline(Func<string, bool> handler, int maxAttempts)
public string Deliver(string messageId, string body)
hints: A `for` loop over attempts; return as soon as the handler succeeds.
In `Replay`, copy the list first, clear it, then call `Deliver` for each entry (it may dead-letter again).
template: if (dojoFailures.TryGetValue(body, out var left) && left > 0) { dojoFailures[body] = left - 1; return false; }
Dojo.Eq("dead letter keeps id and body", new List<string> { "m3: broken" }, dojoPipe.DeadLetters);
Dojo.Eq("replay after the fix", "ok after 1", dojoPipe.Replay());
Dojo.Eq("replayed message now counts as delivered", "duplicate", dojoPipe.Deliver("m3", "broken"));
